1. **Core rule implementation (valid-req-reference)** - File: `src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts` - Implements deep validation that `@req` and `@supports` annotations reference actual requirements in story files. - Key behaviors: - Parses comments for `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports`: - `extractStoryPath(comment)` locates `@story` lines and extracts the story path. - `handleAnnotationLine` dispatches `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` lines to the appropriate handlers. - `processCommentLines` and `processAllComments` iterate over all comment blocks in a file. - Deep requirement parsing & matching: - `loadAndCacheRequirements` reads a story file and extracts all `REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+` tokens via `const regex = /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g;` and caches them by resolved path. - `validateReqLine`: - Extracts the requirement ID from `@req` lines (`extractReqIdFromLine`). - Resolves story path and loads requirements via `resolveStoryAndRequirements`. - Uses `checkRequirementExists` to report `reqMissing` when a requirement is absent. - `parseImplementsLine` and `validateImplementsLine` perform equivalent checks for `@supports ...` annotations. - Path validation and safety: - `validateAndResolveStoryPath` rejects `..` path traversal and absolute paths, reporting `invalidPath`: ```ts if (storyPath.includes("..") || path.isAbsolute(storyPath)) { context.report({ messageId: "invalidPath", data: { storyPath } }); return null; } ``` - Ensures resolved path stays within `cwd`. - Caching: - Uses `const reqCache = new Map<string, Set>();` in `programListener` and populates it in `loadAndCacheRequirements`, avoiding re-reading the same story file multiple times. - Error messages (user experience / error reporting): - `reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'"` - `invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'"` - Both messages are annotated to `docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md` and `docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md`, aligning with REQ-DEEP-ERROR / error-reporting stories. - Rule is wired into ESLint lifecycle via `create(context) { return { Program: programListener(context) }; }`.

5. **Story file alignment** - Story: `docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md` lists: - **REQ-DEEP-PARSE**: Fully implemented via file reading + regex over whole markdown content; tested on standard and bullet-format files. - **REQ-DEEP-MATCH**: Implemented via `checkRequirementExists` and related helpers; tested through multiple valid/invalid scenarios. - **REQ-DEEP-FORMAT**: Implementation is format-agnostic and works across plain text, bullets, and other markdown structures by matching `REQ-...` tokens anywhere in the file; fixtures demonstrate at least two distinct formats (core story and bullet list), and numbered lists or checkbox items would also contain the same `REQ-...` tokens and therefore be supported by the same mechanism. - **REQ-DEEP-SECTION**: The parser does not depend on specific section headings; it scans the entire file content, so requirements in any section (Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, etc.) are handled uniformly. It complements existing file-existence validation by adding content-level checks. - **User Experience**: Implemented and tested. - Error messages are precise and include both the missing requirement ID and the story path; tests assert `messageId` and `data` values, and docs explain these behaviors. - **Error Handling**: Implemented in a robust, non-crashing way. - `loadAndCacheRequirements` wraps `fs.readFileSync` in a `try/catch`; on any read/parsing error it records an empty set instead of throwing, so linting continues without crashing even for malformed or unreadable files. - Because requirement extraction is regex-based and not dependent on markdown structure, malformed markdown and missing sections do not cause parse errors. - **Documentation**: Implemented. - `docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md` documents behavior and includes multiple usage examples, including different annotation patterns and path edge cases.
